title: Where AI models run in Europe
note: Curated by the OpenNodes project from public sources (ONP-2 §3a): the EU/EEA, Switzerland and the UK. documented = the provider's own dated page; claimed = provider statements or news reports. A model is listed at a site only when the provider says it is processed there (no cross-region, Global or Data Zone routing). Corrections by pull request.

providers.name: Amazon Bedrock (European regions)
providers.note: Only models marked In-Region (bedrock-runtime or bedrock-mantle) in the Bedrock model/Region table are listed; models that reach these regions only through EU Geo or Global cross-region inference (e.g. Claude Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5/5.1, Mythos 5.1, Opus 4.5, Nova 2 Lite, OpenAI GPT-5.x/6, Grok, Kimi K3, GLM 5.3) are not listed. Also excluded: models in Legacy or EOL state on the Bedrock lifecycle page (e.g. Claude 3 Haiku, Gemma 3, Llama 3, Mistral 7B/Mixtral, Voxtral, Devstral 2, MiniMax M2/M2.1, DeepSeek-V3.1, Qwen3 Coder 30B/480B, GLM 4.7, Nemotron Nano v2) and speech-only models (Nova 2 Sonic, Nova 2.5 Sonic in eu-north-1).

sites.note: Only an embedding model (Titan Text Embeddings V2) is processed in-region; chat models reach this region only through EU/Global cross-region inference.

AWS names the region only 'Spain'; its data centres are in Aragon. Only an embedding model (Titan Text Embeddings V2) is processed in-region; chat models reach this region only through EU/Global cross-region inference.

Separate aws-eusc partition, generally available since 14 January 2026. Nova Pro and Nova Lite are In-Region in the ESC model table; Gemma 4 (31B, 26B-A4B, E2B) is stated by AWS to run entirely within eusc-de-east-1 (AWS Security Blog, 17 September 2026: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/run-open-weight-models-on-aws-bedrock-in-aws-european-sovereign-cloud/). The exact site in Brandenburg is not published; coordinates are the state centre.

providers.name: Google Vertex AI / Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (European regions)
providers.note: A model is listed only where Google's data-residency page marks in-country ML processing for that region and the locations page shows a regional endpoint there; models processed only within the 'eu' multi-region or via the global endpoint (most Gemini 3.x models, Gemini Embedding, Claude Opus 4.7+ and all Claude 5.x, all MaaS open models) are excluded, as are Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash/Flash-Lite (retired 20 October 2026), deprecated Claude 3.x, Mistral Large (24.07) and Codestral (24.05) (no longer in Google's Mistral model list), E5 embeddings (retired 21 October 2026) and speech models (Chirp, TTS).

sites.note: Claude models are listed here per Google's data-residency table (in-country processing in Belgium); the individual Claude model cards (updated 2026-10-30) instead state 'Europe: Multi-region' ML processing, so this listing should be re-checked.

providers.name: Azure OpenAI in Foundry (European regions)
providers.note: Only the Standard/Regional deployment type (processed in the deployment's region) is counted; models offered in Europe only via Global Standard, Data Zone Standard (EU) or provisioned (incl. regional provisioned) deployments are excluded, as are all non-OpenAI Foundry models (no Standard/Regional option in Europe) and audio models (tts, tts-hd, whisper). Physical locations come from the Azure regions list; GPT-4o merges versions 2024-05-13/2024-08-06 (Sweden Central only) and 2024-11-20.

providers.name: Oracle OCI Generative AI (European regions)
providers.note: Only models hosted on-demand in the region are listed; dedicated-AI-cluster-only models (e.g. Command A Reasoning, Llama 4 Maverick/Scout in London, Rerank 3.5, gpt-oss in London) are excluded, as are Google Gemini 2.5 models in Frankfurt (hosted externally by Google, requests routed to a Google EU location). Other OCI EU regions (Amsterdam, Paris, Madrid, Stockholm, Zurich, Milan, Marseille, Newport) have no local model processing and route calls to Frankfurt or London, so they are not sites.

sites.note: EU Sovereign Cloud realm (OC19), restricted to eligible EU customers; only Llama 3.3 70B (Dynamic FP8) is on-demand, other models are dedicated-cluster only.
UK Government realm (OC4); only Llama 3.3 70B (Dynamic FP8) is on-demand, other models are dedicated-cluster only.

providers.name: IBM watsonx.ai (European regions)
providers.note: Lists the multitenant ready-to-use foundation models and encoder (embedding) models hosted in each region; models marked deprecated, Granite TTM time-series models, and the roughly 70 deploy-on-demand (dedicated) models offered in Frankfurt (none in London) are excluded.

providers.name: Mistral AI (La Plateforme API)
providers.note: The EU endpoint (api.eu.mistral.ai) is served from 'multiple data centers in EU and EFTA countries' that Mistral does not name; api.mistral.ai has no committed location and api.us.mistral.ai runs in the US. Only Mistral's own named sites are listed here.

sites.note: 10 MW site 'dedicated to inference operations', scheduled to open in Q3 2026; no confirmation found that it has opened.

44 MW, about 13,800 Nvidia GB300, financed by $830M of debt (March 2026). The press calls it a training cluster and reported it operational in June 2026 (techdefused.com, 18 Jun 2026). Mistral's own pages do not name it or say which API traffic it serves.

Mistral's page lists 'Sweden site (EcoDataCenter) in motion'. The EcoDataCenter release names Borlänge and gives an opening in 2027 for 'development and operation' of Mistral models: https://ecodatacenter.tech/press/mistral-ai-and-ecodatacenter-partner-to-build-ai-focused-data-center-in-sweden-3431886

providers.models_note: Mistral publishes a model catalogue (including third-party GLM and DeepSeek models) and an EU regional endpoint, but does not say which site serves which model; the named sites are planned or training-focused.

providers.name: Scaleway Generative APIs (Serverless)
providers.note: Read from Scaleway's docs source (scaleway/docs-content). The docs site refused automated fetches. Only models marked 'Available in Serverless' and not past their end-of-life date are listed. Dedicated Deployments are left out.

sites.note: FAQ: 'All Serverless models are currently hosted in a secure data center located in Paris, France, operated by OPCORE'. Scaleway may add other European sites later.

providers.name: OVHcloud AI Endpoints
providers.note: The catalogue says it has 22 models, but only 17 could be read from the page. The current product page says only 'hosted and run in the European Union'. Gravelines comes from OVHcloud's launch release.

sites.note: OVHcloud release of 29 April 2025: 'deployed from the Gravelines datacenter'.

providers.name: IONOS AI Model Hub

residency.statement: All processing occurs only in IONOS German data centres (Berlin), no cross-region replication; prompts and outputs discarded after each request; never used for training.

providers.note: Endpoint openai.inference.de-txl.ionos.com. Paraphrase Multilingual MPNet v2 and FLUX.1-schnell are deprecated and leave the hub on 30 November 2026.

sites.note: 'All processing occurs exclusively in IONOS CLOUD German data centers (Berlin)'; no cross-region replication.

providers.name: STACKIT AI Model Serving
providers.note: Every shared model is priced in region EU01, and the endpoint is api.openai-compat.model-serving.eu01.onstackit.cloud. No AI Model Serving was found documented for the Austrian region eu02.

sites.note: STACKIT: 'all regions exclusively in Germany (eu01) and Austria (eu02)'; the price list labels EU01 Germany South. STACKIT's publicly named German data centres are DC01 Neckarsulm and DC08 Ellhofen (https://stackit.com/en/facts), both near Heilbronn, but it does not say which of them serve AI Model Serving. The point marks that area.

providers.name: T-Systems AI Foundation Services (LLM Hub)

residency.programme: Models hosted on T Cloud Public
residency.statement: Open-weight models are hosted on T Cloud Public, Telekom's sovereign infrastructure in Germany.
OpenAI models run on Microsoft Azure EU regions and Gemini models on Google Cloud EU regions. No region stated for Claude models.

providers.note: Only the models 'Hosted on T-Cloud Public — Telekom's sovereign infrastructure in Germany' are listed. The hub's Azure and GCP models (GPT, Claude, Gemini, in 'EU regions' or unstated regions) are left out, and so is 'd3', whose developer is not named.

sites.note: LLM Hub names only the country. T Cloud Public (formerly Open Telekom Cloud) runs its German region eu-de from the Magdeburg/Biere twin-core data centres (https://open-telekom-cloud.com/en/security/data-centers), but LLM Hub does not name the facility.

providers.name: Nebius Token Factory
providers.note: Public serverless endpoints show Region 'Global': Nebius says the processing location is decided dynamically and can change without notice. Only dedicated endpoints are pinned to a user-selected region. Token Factory docs use eu-north1 (Finland) as the dedicated-endpoint region in their deploy example. Nebius's regions page lists eu-north1 as Finland without naming a city; Mäntsälä is Nebius's own Finnish data centre per its newsroom, so the eu-north1 = Mäntsälä mapping is inferred.

sites.note: Dedicated endpoints only (region eu-north1, Finland per https://docs.nebius.com/overview/regions). City from https://nebius.com/newsroom/nebius-to-triple-capacity-at-finland-data-center-to-75-mw.
A third-party integration guide lists eu-west1 as a dedicated-endpoint region. Nebius's own regions page lists eu-west1 as France with no city, and Token Factory docs don't list it.

providers.models_note: No per-region model mapping. The serverless catalogue is global and not tied to a site. Dedicated endpoints deploy any model from the endpoint-template list, which Nebius says is the source of truth for model/GPU/region combinations, into the chosen region.

providers.name: Infomaniak AI Services
providers.note: Infomaniak says its AI and GPU services run in its own data centres in Switzerland and doesn't name the site for the API. Its Euria press release (Dec 2025) names the D4 data centre (Geneva area) as the one powering Euria, its assistant. Whisper V3 (speech-to-text) is offered too but left out because no modality value fits.

sites.note: Infomaniak's support guide says the AI is hosted only on its own servers in Switzerland (https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1369/understanding-the-use-of-ai-at-infomaniak).

providers.name: Regolo.ai
providers.note: Regolo is Seeweb's inference platform. It says its inference infrastructure is physically hosted in data centres in the Province of Frosinone (Lazio) and in Lombardy, plus unspecified further regions via DHH S.p.A.

sites.note: Regolo names only the region. Seeweb's Lombardy facilities are reported in Milan and Sesto San Giovanni, which Regolo doesn't confirm.

providers.models_note: No per-site mapping. The public catalogue (https://api.regolo.ai/models, checked 2026-11-02) lists apertus-70b, deepseek-ocr-2, gemma4-31b, glm5.2, gpt-oss-120b, gpt-oss-20b, mistral-small-4-119b, qwen3.5-122b, qwen3.5-9b, qwen3.8-27b, Qwen-Image, Qwen3-Embedding-8B and Qwen3-Reranker-4B. It also lists faster-whisper-large-v3 (speech) and Regolo's own brick-v1-beta and clef-flash.

providers.name: Berget AI
providers.note: Berget says it runs on its own hardware in Sweden. A second data centre in Southern Stockholm went live in March 2026 (https://berget.ai/en/blog/second-datacenter-is-live). The original site's city isn't named, so both sites are recorded as one country-level site. Speech-to-text models (KB-Whisper, NB-Whisper, Pianissimo, faster-whisper) and preview/eval 'system-one' models are left out.

providers.name: Swisscom Swiss AI Platform

residency.statement: Swisscom says data and information remain in Switzerland at all times, with processing and storage in Switzerland. Retention not described.

providers.note: Enterprise offer with managed inference endpoints through the Swisscom Digital Marketplace. Swisscom says data stays in Switzerland but names no data-centre city. Apertus is the only model it names; other multimodal, speech-to-text and LLM models are mentioned without names.

providers.name: Exoscale AI Inference

residency.statement: Dedicated Inference: data never leaves Europe; runs in EU and Swiss GPU zones. On-Demand preview runs only in AT-VIE-2 (Vienna). Prompts and responses not stored; not used for training.

providers.note: There are two products. On-Demand Inference is a per-token model catalogue, in private preview by invitation, and runs only in AT-VIE-2 (Vienna). Dedicated Inference (GA since 15 June 2026) runs bring-your-own Hugging Face models on dedicated GPUs in the GPU zones, which the product page gives as examples: AT-VIE-2, CH-GVA-2, DE-FRA-1, HR-ZAG-1, CH-DK-2. Dedicated Inference has no fixed catalogue, so models are attached only to AT-VIE-2. Zone cities are from https://www.exoscale.com/datacenters/.

sites.note: On-Demand Inference (private preview) and Dedicated Inference.
Dedicated Inference only (bring your own model).
Dedicated Inference only (bring your own model).
Dedicated Inference only (bring your own model).
Dedicated Inference only (bring your own model).

providers.name: GreenPT API
providers.note: GreenPT says the platform is hosted by Scaleway in Paris and that its Code models (GLM-5.3, Kimi K2.7 Code) run in Verda data centres in Helsinki. It does not say where the other models run, so they are listed without a site. Left out: MiniMax (conflicting statements), Deepgram speech models, Metis, the green-* aliases and models marked "Older".

sites.note: Scaleway (location code PAR).
Verda data centres FIN-01, FIN-02 and FIN-03.

providers.name: Groq (Helsinki)
providers.note: Groq's first European footprint, in space leased from Equinix (the facility among Equinix's Helsinki sites is not stated). GroqCloud docs say customer data is retained in GCP buckets in the United States; there is no documented EU region selection.

sites.note: Announced 6 July 2025; reachable over Equinix Fabric private connections

providers.models_note: Groq does not say which GroqCloud models are served from Helsinki, and its data page (https://console.groq.com/docs/your-data) mentions no European region.

providers.name: Cerebras Inference (Europe, planned)
providers.note: July 2026: Cerebras says its first European capacity comes online by end of 2026, scaling to 200 MW across France and the Nordics by end of 2027; part of it is for OpenAI workloads. No European site is confirmed live. The University of Edinburgh (EPCC) CS-3 cluster is a research system, not Cerebras Inference, and is left out.

sites.note: Announced 1 September 2026; 165 MW in phases, first 50 MW under construction
Country only; part of the 200 MW European build-out announced July 2026
Country only; capacity contracted for 2027

providers.models_note: No European site is live yet, and Cerebras names no models for its European capacity.

providers.name: Nscale (Norway, UK)
providers.note: Nscale sells GPU capacity and also runs a serverless inference API, but it does not say which site serves it. Partner sites listed by Nscale (Stavanger, Oslo, Hayes, Sines, Keflavik, Blönduós) are left out because their status is not stated.

sites.note: 30 MW operational, expandable to 60 MW
Designed for 230 MW. Announced July 2025 with Aker and OpenAI; in 2026 Microsoft contracted the capacity after OpenAI reportedly withdrew. No confirmed go-live.
Up to 90 MW; press reports a Q4 2026 go-live

providers.models_note: GPU capacity for customers. Nscale's serverless inference models are not tied to any site, and its model docs require an access code.

providers.name: LUMI AI Factory (Kajaani)

residency.statement: Aitta processes requests on LUMI nodes but publishes no residency, retention or logging terms; use is governed by Aitta's terms of use and LUMI project access.

providers.note: EuroHPC AI Factory. Aitta is an OpenAI-compatible inference service on LUMI-G nodes (2 nodes), open to LUMI project users and not meant for production. LUMI-AI, a new system in the same Kajaani data centre, is due in the second half of 2027.

sites.note: LUMI is located in CSC's Kajaani data centre (https://www.lumi-supercomputer.eu/lumi-ai-factory-first-services/)

providers.name: JUPITER AI Factory (Jülich)

residency.statement: No statement on where user data is processed or stored; access policy not published.

providers.note: EuroHPC AI Factory on JUPITER. It lists a Model Deployment service, and JUPITER is to be extended with the JARVIS inference system (https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101250682). JARVIS was put to tender in July 2026, with the contract due to start in March 2027.

sites.note: Planned refers to the JARVIS inference service; JUPITER itself is in operation

providers.models_note: Models not published; the inference system is still being procured.

providers.name: HammerHAI AI Factory (Stuttgart)

residency.statement: HLRS says the HammerHAI system will be operated in Germany in line with EU data-security rules. A location statement for the planned system, not detailed data terms.

providers.note: EuroHPC AI Factory open since April 2025. It already offers startups and SMEs access to LLM inference services, on existing systems hosted by consortium partners, without saying which. The dedicated HammerHAI system (HPE, NVIDIA GB200 NVL4, Axelera AI inference partition) is due in operation in the second half of 2026.

sites.note: Delivery scheduled for Q2 2026, operation for H2 2026; later moving to the new HLRS III building. Go-live not confirmed.

providers.models_note: No model list published for HammerHAI's LLM inference services.

providers.name: IT4LIA AI Factory (Bologna)

residency.statement: Speaks of compliance with EU data sovereignty and privacy standards, but does not say where user data is processed or stored.

providers.note: EuroHPC AI Factory. It has offered AI compute on Leonardo since April 2025. The new AI-optimised system (contract signed April 2026) has a dedicated European partition with Axelera AI accelerators for AI inference.

sites.note: Planned refers to the inference partition; no installation date published

providers.models_note: Models not published; no hosted model service documented yet.

providers.name: BSC AI Factory (Barcelona)

residency.statement: Only access-level policies are mentioned; nothing on data residency or processing location.

providers.note: EuroHPC AI Factory. MareNostrum 5 is being upgraded with AI partitions 'specially designed' for LLM training and inference (contract signed January 2026). No hosted model service is described.

sites.note: Planned refers to the AI partitions; MareNostrum 5 itself is in operation

providers.models_note: Compute for inference workloads; no hosted model API and no models published.

providers.name: Deutsche Telekom Industrial AI Cloud (Munich)

residency.statement: Telekom says the AI factory is operated on German soil under strict data-protection requirements; no product-level residency terms published.

sites.note: In operation since 4 February 2026. Telekom said (Nov 2025) that Perplexity would use it for in-country inference.

providers.models_note: GPU capacity (about 10,000 NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, with data-centre partner Polarise); no public list of models served there. Telekom's hosted models are listed under T-Systems AI Foundation Services.

sites.note: Stated in the node's own card description (Hetzner CPX22 VM).
